name: Aeneas
personality:
If George were to be the matured, older brother of the Guardians of Chroma, Aeneas would be the younger, immature sibling. 

Most of the time, he tends to jump to conclusions, or rush important things. Sometimes, he might get lost who-knows-where and George will have to find him, and help him find his way back. His heart’s still in the right place, though! As long as everyone holds hands and gets along, there’s no reason he should give up anytime soon! After all, he’s got responsibilities as a guardian!

abilities.name: Grass
abilities.description: More in tune with plantlife, able to nurture and control its growth to fit desires.

abilities.name: Crystalline Artwork
abilities.description: Aeneas can create sculptures of sugar in his free time. These are works of art, but they can be eaten.

abilities.name: Effect Spore
abilities.description: Contact with the Pokémon may inflict poison, sleep, or paralysis on the attacker.

abilities.name: Sugarapple
abilities.description:
When any status is inflicted on anyone, Aeneas gains a stack of Sugarslice, up to five, with a limit of once per action. 
When reaching max Sugarslice stacks, combine them to form a Sugarapple. Aeneas cannot gain Sugarslice if he has a Sugarapple.
With a Sugarapple, Aeneas using a damaging move follows up with an additional move on the same target known as Sugar Bomb. Sugar Bomb cannot be used any other way.

abilities.name: Terastal Mastery
abilities.description:
Allows Aeneas to enter into his Terastal Form, and with great, taxing burden on himself, his Stellar Form. 
When in either form, his Normal Type becomes the Stellar Type. 
When in the Terastal or Stellar Form, Sugar Bomb is enhanced. For every ally above half health or terastallized or mini-terastallized (same ally can count twice if they fill multiple conditions), it deals 10% more damage.
When in the Stellar Form, all of Aeneas’s stats (except speed) are raised 2 stages, and he takes notable damage every time he uses a move (excluding Sugar Bomb) for as long as he remains in Stellar Form. 
If Aeneas drops below half health, he automatically returns to his Normal Form.

moves.name: Energy Ball
moves.description: The user attacks by drawing power from nature and firing it at targets. This may also lower targets’ Sp. Def stats.

moves.name: Dragon Pulse
moves.description: The target is attacked with a shock wave generated by the user’s gaping mouth. This attack never misses.

moves.name: Dragon Cheer
moves.description: The user raises its allies’ morale with a draconic cry so that their future attacks have a heightened chance of landing critical hits. This rouses Dragon types more.

moves.name: Aromatherapy
moves.description: A soothing scent is released to heal all status problems in the user’s party.

moves.name: Trailblaze
moves.description: The user attacks suddenly as if leaping out from tall grass. The user’s nimble footwork boosts its Speed stat.

moves.name: Tera Starstorm
moves.description: With the power of its crystals, the user bombards and eliminates the target. When used by Terapagos in its Stellar Form, this move damages all opposing Pokémon.

moves.name: Sugar Shatter
moves.description: Sugar is shattered to hit all enemies, inflicting on each enemy either poison, sleep, paralysis, or nothing.

moves.name: Sugarbomb
moves.description: The Sugarapple is launched at the target and explodes in a wonderful mess of crystals.

backstory:
Sugar and spice and then everything nice, colors as red as the skin of a fruit,
Sparks with timber lead to a flame, burning as orange as wonderfully tamed,
Leading the pie to be wonderfully crisp, yellowly golden to sweeten the eyes,
Bringing it outside to dine in the sun, a lovely field of green surrounding the pie,
Looking above we see the sky, blue and cloudy as all can’t deny,
Eating and eating we all spend our day, till night comes with its purple tinted skies!
...
Terapagos wasn’t ever the best with rhymes. For all that was confusing, he’d mysteriously awoken one day having dreamed of baking a pie.
... It didn’t help that the pie from his dream smelled delicious. The sort of smell you’d smell after a long day playing outside, where the sun shone onto you from above, the birds chirped and sang in the trees, and your mother happily called, announcing she’d baked a treat for you and your friends.
...
Oddly enough, he felt like he was the pie. It was an incredible stretch of logic, but...
He just felt... sweeter than usual. More carefree. Like that concept of that day outside, the sun shining, the birds, the allure of pie...
He didn’t feel like a participant in that scene. He felt like... the scene itself.
...
He felt like an apple. 
He felt like a bag of sugar.
He felt like both could combine into a sweet, sugary apple.
...
And from that sugary apple, could there be a refined, sweeter, sugar. 
And when that sugar was melted, it could create stellar, crystal treats. 
...
But Aeneas honestly just wanted some plain old apple pie.
